summary: Java written for all 53 requirements (single controller, 5 modes, every transition triggered by the per-cycle TransmissionReceived event, terminal emergency stop). Nothing is unimplemented; 14 choices the requirements do not settle are listed.

issues.title: Numeric values of the boiler, steam and pump constants
issues.raw: SB-DM1, SB-DM2 and SB-DM3 name C, M1, M2, N1, N2, W, U1, U2 and P but give no values.
issues.fix_directive: Chosen: C=1000, M1=150, M2=850, N1=400, N2=600 (litres), W=25 (l/s), U1=U2=2 (l/s/s), P=10 (l/s), cycle 5 s, 4 pumps, STOP limit 3. All are integral, so the model's rounding of fractional constants does not change any guard. Replace them with the plant's real values if known.

issues.title: Pump numbering and the pump returned when none qualifies
issues.raw: The messages name pump n without fixing the numbering; pumpToOpen()/pumpToClose() need a value of their declared (nat) type even when no pump qualifies.
issues.fix_directive: Pumps are numbered 1..4. pumpToOpen() returns 1 and pumpToClose() returns 4 when no pump qualifies; the controller only uses them under the guards openablePumpCount() > 0 / closablePumpCount() > 0, so the defaults are never transmitted.

issues.title: One per-cycle trigger event; the transmission's contents are read through the sensor
issues.raw: SB-V3: all incoming messages of a cycle are received simultaneously, but step(InputEvent) takes one event.
issues.fix_directive: Added InputEvent.TransmissionReceived (not a physical-unit message) as the trigger of every transition: the cycle driver buffers the cycle's messages in BoilerSensor, analyses them, then calls step(TransmissionReceived). Every transition is event-triggered, so the model has no autonomous transition cycle (no divergence), and every non-terminal mode has a catch-all branch.

issues.title: Variables q, v, p, the level estimate, unit status and STOP count live in the sensor layer
issues.raw: SB-V5..SB-V10 are variables; the profile allows guards to use sensor calls, constants and predicates.
issues.fix_directive: The controller's only state is its mode. q, v, p, the estimate bounds and the STOP count are fields of BoilerSensor; the per-unit status (out of order / announcement awaiting acknowledgement) is kept in UnitStatusBoard. The controller reads them through sensor methods, which the model treats as functions.

issues.title: Failure announcements and repair acknowledgements are emitted by the unit-status board, not by step()
issues.raw: SB-FR6/SB-FR7: a variable set of per-unit messages each cycle, repeated until acknowledged.
issues.fix_directive: UnitStatusBoard.protocolMessages() builds, each cycle, every failure detection not yet acknowledged and the acknowledgement of each repair received in the cycle; the cycle driver transmits them with the controller's messages. They are therefore not part of the extracted state machine. After emergency stop nothing more is transmitted.

issues.title: Pump regulation law
issues.raw: SB-Beh10/SB-Beh15/SB-Beh19 require keeping the level in [N1, N2] by switching pumps but fix no control law.
issues.fix_directive: Each cycle at most one pump is changed: close one when the worst-case forecast maximum exceeds N2 (and the minimum does not fall below N1), open one in the symmetric case, otherwise hold. A cycle that changes mode holds the pumps (safe for that cycle because the level-risk check already covers the coming cycle).

issues.title: Level risk (SB-Beh13/18/21) judged on a worst-case forecast of the coming cycle
issues.raw: The requirements say 'risks reaching M1 or M2 under worst-case behaviour' without a formula.
issues.fix_directive: Forecast = current level bounds (q, or the estimate) minus worst-case steam over 5 s (rate bounded by W, U1, U2) plus pumps surely/possibly pouring (a pump counts as surely pouring only once its controller confirms flow; newly ordered pumps pour nothing for one cycle, SB-Beh25). Risk = forecast min <= M1 or forecast max >= M2. The same bounds give the expected range for the level-device dynamic check (SB-FR3) and, while the device is out of order, the estimate (SB-V8).

issues.title: What counts as an aberrant message (SB-FR5)
issues.raw: SB-FR5 says 'a message whose presence is aberrant' without listing them.
issues.fix_directive: Aberrant: a data message duplicated for the same unit; a pump number outside 1..4; STEAM_BOILER_WAITING after initialization; PHYSICAL_UNITS_READY outside initialization or before PROGRAM_READY was sent; a repair message for a unit not out of order; a failure acknowledgement for a unit with no announcement pending. Missing: any of LEVEL, STEAM, or PUMP_STATE / PUMP_CONTROL_STATE for any of the four pumps.

issues.title: Initialization procedure details
issues.raw: SB-Beh4/5/7 say drain above N2, fill below N1, announce PROGRAM_READY once within [N1, N2]; the valve's flow rate is not given.
issues.fix_directive: Above N2: send VALVE to open the valve if closed. Below N1: close the valve if open, else open one pump if none is on. Within [N1, N2]: close the valve or the filling pump if needed and send PROGRAM_READY, every cycle until PHYSICAL_UNITS_READY. While the valve is open the level-device dynamic check has no lower bound (drain rate unknown). In initialization a non-zero steam reading after STEAM_BOILER_WAITING also marks the steam device out of order.

issues.title: MODE(m) payload is a separate enum ModeIndicator
issues.raw: SB-DM10: the mode is a five-valued datum carried by MODE(m); the controller's mode enum is also its states.
issues.fix_directive: ModeIndicator (INITIALIZATION_MODE ... EMERGENCY_STOP_MODE) is the message payload; BoilerMode is the controller's state enum. Kept apart so that enumeration literals and state names do not clash.

issues.title: Emergency stop is terminal versus MODE(m) on every cycle
issues.raw: SB-Beh22: on entering emergency stop the program stops. SB-Beh24: MODE(m) is sent on every cycle in whatever mode.
issues.fix_directive: EMERGENCY_STOP has no outgoing transition. MODE(emergency_stop) is sent once, in the cycle that enters it; afterwards the program has stopped and transmits nothing.

issues.title: 'Nothing else happens' before STEAM_BOILER_WAITING
issues.raw: SB-Beh2 says nothing else happens until STEAM_BOILER_WAITING arrives; SB-Beh9 and SB-Beh23 demand emergency stop on transmission failure and on three STOPs during initialization.
issues.fix_directive: Operator stop and transmission failure lead to emergency stop even before STEAM_BOILER_WAITING; everything else (steam check, level failure, filling, draining) waits for it.

issues.title: Level failure together with a steam or pump-controller failure outside rescue mode
issues.raw: SB-Beh11/SB-Beh17 send a level failure to rescue; SB-Beh21 stops rescue on steam or pump-controller failure; SB-FR8 orders simultaneous consequences.
issues.fix_directive: In normal and degraded mode a level failure while the steam device or a pump controller is out of order goes directly to emergency stop (the rescue estimate would be untrustworthy at once). 'The pump-controller units fail' (SB-Beh21) is read as: any pump controller out of order.

issues.title: STOP count saturates at the stop limit; p counts pumps with flow observed
issues.raw: SB-V10 describes the count without a bound; SB-V7 derives p without a formula.
issues.fix_directive: The STOP count stops growing at 3 (emergency stop is entered at 3). p = P x number of pumps reported on whose controller reports flow.

next_step: Run the pipeline. The listed items are decisions to review, not known defects.
